clue.text: A sort of adjustable spanner

parts.note: a spanner here is a bridge spanning a moat, and this kind can be raised and lowered, so it is adjustable

explanation.surface: A description of a workshop tool for gripping nuts of different sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle's raising bridge across a moat is literally a span that can be adjusted up or down.

clue.text: Act of one journalist upset another

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word for the journalist upside down, so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: ED is the usual crossword abbreviation for editor, a journalist
a second journalist, again ED for editor

explanation.surface: One newspaper editor's action tipped another into distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the first ED into DE, which is followed by the second ED.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is a thing done, an action, the same sense as an act.

clue.text: Theologian, one into NT book, gets folk very enthusiastic

indicators.note: into says the theologian and the one go inside the book's name

parts.note: Acts is a book of the New Testament
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar studying a New Testament book wins over keen followers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is only a link; 'very enthusiastic' qualifies 'folk', so the definition is the whole phrase, describing devotees.
explanation.definitionFit: Addicts in the loose sense are fans, people wildly keen on something.

clue.text: Person at sales unearthing bra with unusual design

indicators.note: an unusual design means the letters of the two words are laid out in a new pattern

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopper at the sales digs out a bra of an odd style.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at the sales looks for cheap deals, which is what a seeker of bargains does.

clue.text: Poor home with little woman and little man

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
Di is a short form of the woman's name Diana
gent is the short form of gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A hard-up household with a small wife and a small husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigent is a formal synonym for destitute, lacking money.

clue.text: Good American to manifest great enjoyment

parts.note: US stands for United States, so American
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fine American shows how much they are enjoying themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manifest' is only a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is relish or zest, keen enjoyment of something.

clue.text: Ruler captured by cameras turning back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
captured by says the letters are held inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A monarch caught on film by cameras swinging round to face behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Ruler captured' as the definition, but 'captured by' is the hiding signal; the definition is 'Ruler' alone. RAST read 'back' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was an emperor of Russia, a sovereign ruler.

clue.text: Affair makes the woman get a particular hairstyle

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
bangs is the American term for a fringe of hair cut straight across

explanation.surface: A woman is told she has to have a certain haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole shebang means the whole business or matter, an affair in the sense of a thing.

clue.text: Ruddy optimistic

definitions.meaning: literally tinged with a pinkish red colour
seeing things too favourably, as through coloured glasses

explanation.definitionFit: The compound means both tinted pink-red and, through the idiom of coloured spectacles, hopeful.

clue.text: Bird? Don't let 'er be seen, we say

indicators.note: we say signals that the words are spoken, here in a dropped-aitch accent

parts.note: keep her out of sight is hide her, which with the aitches dropped like 'er becomes 'ide 'er

explanation.surface: A protective instruction to keep a woman out of view.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'er hints that the h is dropped, so hide her is said 'ide 'er.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck, the source of eiderdown.

clue.text: Terrible events that could make sister sad

indicators.note: could make says these words can be rearranged into something else

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tragedies that might upset a sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: Disasters are catastrophes, dreadful happenings.

clue.text: New Catholics miss medieval sort of philosophy

indicators.note: new says the letters of the two words take a fresh form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Recent converts to Catholicism overlook a branch of medieval thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholasticism was the system of theology and philosophy taught in medieval universities.

clue.text: Transplant operation? A different attitude coming about

definitions.meaning: literally swapping one heart for another, the question mark flagging the whimsy
a shift of opinion or feeling

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a change of mind, and taken literally names a new heart being fitted.

clue.text: Fussy detail

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adjective for fastidious and as a noun for a specific item.

clue.text: Donkey getting on with smaller animal making similar sounds

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
taken as written
an ant is a much smaller creature than a donkey

explanation.surface: A donkey getting along with a tiny creature while braying alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Assonant describes words that resemble each other in their vowel sounds, a kind of rhyme.

clue.text: 'Work hard!' — a new rallying cry

parts.note: to slog is to toil

explanation.surface: An exhortation to toil, offered as a fresh motto.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a catchphrase, originally a Gaelic war cry.

clue.text: Bird that's cherished, with an inclination to be protected

indicators.note: being protected means held inside, so these letters sit within the cherished word

parts.note: a pet is a cherished favourite
an gives the single letter A
rake is a slope or slant, as of a stage

explanation.surface: A beloved creature that tends to need sheltering.
explanation.definitionFit: A parakeet is a small long-tailed parrot.

clue.text: Go wrong in journey to the north?

parts.note: a trip is a journey
up means northwards, as in going up to Scotland

explanation.surface: Making a mistake during a trip northwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip up is to stumble or make an error.

clue.text: Being wicked, first to last, in part of cricket match

indicators.note: first to last says the opening letter is moved to the end

parts.note: sinning is doing wrong

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing during a phase of a cricket game.
explanation.walkthrough: SINNING with its first S sent to the end. In cricket an innings is a team's or batsman's turn to bat.
explanation.definitionFit: An innings is one side's spell at batting in cricket.

clue.text: Dad's furry animal is OK

parts.note: pa is dad, with the possessive s
the sable is a marten prized for its fur

explanation.surface: Father's fur-bearing pet is fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Passable means adequate, acceptable, all right.

clue.text: Most skeletal one with bits misplaced

indicators.note: misplaced says the letters of these words are out of position

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The thinnest person, whose parts are scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: Boniest is the superlative of bony, meaning thinnest with bones showing.

clue.text: Dismay shown by prisoner put with Eastern sailors in base

parts.note: con is short for convict

indicators.note: in says the eastern and the sailors are placed within the base

parts.note: a station is a base, as for police or military
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Alarm when a convict is quartered with eastern seamen at a naval base.
explanation.definitionFit: Consternation is anxious alarm, the same feeling as dismay.

clue.text: Get up about noon initially and wash

indicators.note: about says the word for getting up goes round the next letter

parts.note: to rise is to get up

indicators.note: initially says only the opening letter of noon is used

explanation.surface: Rise around midday and have a wash.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to wash lightly in clean water.

clue.text: Outdoor party in safe territory

indicators.note: in says the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A garden gathering held on secure ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fund-raising event with stalls and games.

clue.text: Crossing far side of glen, record mountains over a protracted period

indicators.note: the record crosses over the letter, so it holds it inside

parts.note: a log is a record, as a ship's log

indicators.note: far side picks the final letter of glen

parts.note: a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: A walker crossing a valley sets a record over the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-range describes forecasts or plans covering a long time ahead.

clue.text: Anger shown by one lacking love for woman

parts.note: ire is anger

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is taken out of the word one

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Fury from someone who missed out on romance with a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Kind of brown bit of bread about to be chucked

indicators.note: chucked means thrown out, so the abbreviation is removed

parts.note: a crust is the hard outer part of a loaf
c is circa, about

explanation.surface: A browned crust of bread about to be thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust is a reddish-brown shade, the colour of oxidised iron.

clue.text: Recent changes over time to bring non-imperial unit

indicators.note: over says the rearranged letters cover and enclose the next word
changes says the letters of recent are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Modern reforms over the years bring in metric measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' turns RECENT into CENTRE, which goes over TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A centimetre is a metric measure, not one of the old imperial units like inches.
